THE FIZLET™ PERIODIC TABLE / BRICKS

V0.27.0 · 43 SHIPPED · 3 PLANNED · THIS TABLE 1.6 KB gz

Logic & style.
The bricks do the rest.

Every brick is a job we wrote again and again over two decades of animation and game work, solved once and kept small. Bring the logic and the style; take only the bricks you need. 43 shipped, each with its size measured on this build; 3 on the roadmap, dashed.

Every brick, every export Brick stickers The FILET factory ↓

blocks.lead: One small kernel and a box of bricks, each its own import with its own size budget. Each page is generated from the source: the API from the type declarations, the size measured on this build.

items.head: 1krKERNEL
name: @fzlt/
core
items.what: The kernel: one loop, bounded work, and the page always comes back.
items.toy: Tap the floor to drop a brick; tap a brick to knock it out.5.7 KB gz

items.head: 4inCOMPLETE
name: @fzlt/
core/
input
items.what: One controller for keys, pointer and a touch stick, mapped to named intents.
items.toy: Tap to start; whack a brick with a tap or its key (1–4, A S D F).7.5 KB gz

items.head: 12pdCOMPLETE
name: @fzlt/
core/
pad
items.what: Swappable on-screen controls for touch (and mouse).
items.toy: Drive with the stick, the arrows or a tap; SHOVE to dash; SWAP for a d-pad.12.9 KB gz

items.head: 5clCOMPLETE
name: @fzlt/
core/
collide
items.what: A fixed-capacity spatial hash (no allocation per insert or query) and the shape tests games need: circle–circle, circle–rect, swept segment–circle.
items.toy: Tap to fire a ball at that spot.9.7 KB gz

items.head: 10grBETA
name: @fzlt/
core/
grid
items.what: The game board.
items.toy: Tap a cell to walk there; tap a rock to break it.7.5 KB gz

items.head: 6fxCOMPLETE
name: @fzlt/
core/
fx
items.what: Explosions that land.
items.toy: Tap near the crate, or tap the crate.10.3 KB gz

items.head: 19cmBETA
name: @fzlt/
core/
camera
items.what: The page is the camera.
items.toy: Tap anywhere to dive in; tap again to fly back.7.1 KB gz

items.head: 11spCOMPLETE
name: @fzlt/
core/
sprite
items.what: The character layer's drawing primitive.
items.toy: Tap the bug. Four times.7.2 KB gz

items.head: 7snCOMPLETE
name: @fzlt/
core/
sound
items.what: The sound adapter.
items.toy: Tap above the stairs to drop a ball (sound on).6.9 KB gz

items.head: 8emCOMPLETE
name: @fzlt/
core/
embed
items.what: Drop a game onto any page with one small config.
items.toy: Double-tap the card, or type BRICK.8.3 KB gz

items.head: 9slCOMPLETE

core/

items.what: Mount a Fizlet scene into an Astro page engine slot: the element carrying class="ae-slot" data-slot-target="<page>#<slot>" role="img" aria-label="…".
items.toy: Tap to slide the strip on; tap a live scene to drop its brick again.7.8 KB gz

items.head: 13hdBETA
name: @fzlt/
core/
hud
items.what: Change-only HUD bindings that never allocate in the steady state.
items.toy: Tap to strike; tap fast to heat it up and ring the bell.7.7 KB gz

items.head: 15mtBETA
name: @fzlt/
core/
match
items.what: The match flow every game shares, intro → count → play → paused → end, on the Board UI kit's overlay (grey dim, a sticker that slams, at most two sticker keys).
items.toy: Tap to start, then catch the bricks on your paddle.8.7 KB gz

items.head: 16brCOMPLETE
name: @fzlt/
core/
board-page
items.what: The host page as the board.
items.toy: Tap to fire a bite at that spot.13.4 KB gz

items.head: 2uiCOMPLETE
name: @fzlt/
core/
ui
items.what: The tiny behaviour half of board-ui.css.
items.toy: Tap a key to fire a brick along the row, or tap above to drop one.7.0 KB gz

items.head: 18pfCOMPLETE
name: @fzlt/
core/
perf
items.what: A live performance overlay for players, off until they switch it on.
items.toy: Tap high or low to drop a long task.7.6 KB gz

items.head: 17rlCOMPLETE
name: @fzlt/
core/
rules
items.what: The rules every arcade game repeats, as three small systems on the kernel: - waves: a wave clock, prepare → assault → rebuild, with a spawn budget per wave; - drops: pickups that fall, wait to be collected and expire; - score: points, a combo that decays, and levels from XP thresholds.

items.toy: Bring the pointer near, or tap the tower.8.4 KB gz

name: @fzlt/

name: @fzlt/
core/
timeline

items.toy: Tap to make the bricks dance into the next shape.7.9 KB gz

touch

items.toy: Drag the blue brick and let go to throw it.6.1 KB gz

core/
css-clock
items.what: A page's own CSS @keyframes, on the kernel clock.
items.toy: Tap anywhere to scrub the stylesheet's time.8.6 KB gz

blocks.lead: Used in our games. Not a supported multiplayer service. These bricks stay in the package (MIT, with their flags), and our games run them against our own room server, which isn't a hosted service. Build your own room server: the wire protocol, the pattern and a threat checklist.

name: @fzlt/
core/
presence
items.what: Lockstep input exchange for multiplayer, behind a tiny transport adapter.
items.toy: Tap a column on either board to drop a brick.7.4 KB gz

blocks.lead: Fizlet 0.x is a public beta: every brick carries a status flag, and a 0.x minor release may change a BETA brick's API (the CHANGELOG says how). COMPLETE bricks keep theirs. Each brick's page shows its flag and the evidence: the release it shipped in, the games and pages that ship it, and its tests.

sticker.title: Done, and always getting smaller and faster.
sticker.label: COMPLETE

items.line: Done, and always getting smaller and faster.
criteria: Its own export in package.json, with a size budget that npm run size checks in CI
Tests in the suites (Node, and Chromium where it touches the page), including zero allocation per step where it runs per step
Documented: a README row and a generated brick page
Shipped: used by at least one released game or production page beyond its own demo
API stable: no breaking change since it first shipped; one would need a CHANGELOG entry and moves it back to BETA

sticker.title: Tested and budgeted; not yet carried by a shipped game, or its API is still moving.
sticker.label: BETA

items.line: Tested and budgeted; not yet carried by a shipped game, or its API is still moving.
criteria: Its own export, a size budget, tests and docs, like COMPLETE
Not yet used by a released game or production page, or its API is still growing
Safe to build on; a minor release may change it, and the CHANGELOG says how
